SIMPLIFY_FRACTION.title: Simplify the fraction
SIMPLIFY_FRACTION.text: Divide the top and bottom by their greatest common factor to get {result}.

POWER_OF_POWER.title: Multiply the exponents
POWER_OF_POWER.text: Raising a power of {base} to another power means multiplying the exponents.

SIMPLIFY_RADICAL.title: Simplify the square root
SIMPLIFY_RADICAL.text: {radicand} has a square factor, so the root becomes {outside} times the root of {inside}.

MULTIPLY_BY_ZERO.title: Multiply by zero
MULTIPLY_BY_ZERO.text: Anything multiplied by zero is zero.

ZERO_NUMERATOR.title: Zero divided by something
ZERO_NUMERATOR.text: Zero divided by anything other than zero is zero.

REMOVE_ADDITIVE_IDENTITY.title: Drop the zero
REMOVE_ADDITIVE_IDENTITY.text: Adding zero changes nothing, so it can be removed.

REMOVE_MULTIPLICATIVE_IDENTITY.title: Drop the one
REMOVE_MULTIPLICATIVE_IDENTITY.text: Multiplying by one changes nothing, so it can be removed.

POWER_OF_ZERO.title: Power of zero
POWER_OF_ZERO.text: Anything except zero raised to the power zero is one.

POWER_OF_ONE.title: Power of one
POWER_OF_ONE.text: Raising to the power one leaves the value unchanged.

ONE_TO_ANY_POWER.title: One to any power
ONE_TO_ANY_POWER.text: One raised to any power is one.

DIVIDE_BY_ONE.title: Divide by one
DIVIDE_BY_ONE.text: Dividing by one leaves the value unchanged.

COMBINE_LIKE_TERMS.title: Combine like terms
COMBINE_LIKE_TERMS.text: {terms} have the same variable part, so add their coefficients to get {result}.

COLLECT_LIKE_FACTORS.title: Collect the powers
COLLECT_LIKE_FACTORS.text: Multiplying powers of {base} means adding the exponents.

DISTRIBUTE_NEGATIVE.title: Distribute the minus sign
DISTRIBUTE_NEGATIVE.text: A minus sign in front of {sum} flips the sign of every term inside.

EXPAND_POWER.title: Write out the power
EXPAND_POWER.text: {base} to the power {exponent} means {exponent} copies multiplied together.

MULTIPLY_FRACTIONS.title: Multiply the fractions
MULTIPLY_FRACTIONS.text: Multiply the numerators together and the denominators together.

DIVIDE_BY_FRACTION.title: Divide by a fraction
DIVIDE_BY_FRACTION.text: Dividing by {divisor} is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal.

ADD_FRACTIONS.title: Use a common denominator
ADD_FRACTIONS.text: Rewrite both fractions over {denominator}, then add the numerators.

CANCEL_FRACTION_FACTORS.title: Cancel common factors
CANCEL_FRACTION_FACTORS.text: The top and bottom share factors, so cancel them.

SWAP_SIDES.title: Swap the sides
SWAP_SIDES.text: Put the side containing the variable on the left.

CLEAR_DENOMINATORS.title: Multiply both sides by {by}
CLEAR_DENOMINATORS.text: Multiplying both sides by {by} clears the fraction.

MOVE_VARIABLE_TERMS.title: Move the variable terms left
MOVE_VARIABLE_TERMS.text: Move {terms} to the {side} side and change the sign. This is the same as subtracting it from both sides.

MOVE_CONSTANT_TERMS.title: Move the numbers right
MOVE_CONSTANT_TERMS.text: Move {terms} to the {side} side and change the sign. This is the same as subtracting it from both sides.

DIVIDE_BOTH_SIDES.title: Divide both sides by {by}
DIVIDE_BOTH_SIDES.text: Divide both sides by {by} to leave the variable on its own.

MOVE_ALL_TO_LEFT.title: Bring everything to one side
MOVE_ALL_TO_LEFT.text: Move every term to the left so the equation reads: something equals zero.

FACTOR_QUADRATIC.title: Factor the quadratic
FACTOR_QUADRATIC.text: Find two numbers that multiply to {product} and add to {sum}, then write the quadratic as a product.

ZERO_PRODUCT.title: Set each factor to zero
ZERO_PRODUCT.text: A product is zero only when one of its factors is zero, so solve each bracket separately.

QUADRATIC_FORMULA.title: Apply the quadratic formula
QUADRATIC_FORMULA.text: With a = {a}, b = {b} and c = {c}, substitute into the quadratic formula.

QUADRATIC_ROOTS.title: Read off the solutions
QUADRATIC_ROOTS.text: Taking the plus and the minus gives the two solutions.

NO_REAL_SOLUTIONS.title: No real solutions
NO_REAL_SOLUTIONS.text: The discriminant is negative, so this equation has no real solutions.

IDENTITY_TRUE.title: Always true
IDENTITY_TRUE.text: Both sides are identical, so every value of the variable works.

IDENTITY_FALSE.title: Never true
IDENTITY_FALSE.text: The two sides can never be equal, so there is no solution.

DIFF_SUM.title: Differentiate each term separately
DIFF_SUM.text: A sum changes at the combined rate of its parts, so the {count} terms can be handled one at a time.

DIFF_NEGATIVE.title: Take the minus sign outside
DIFF_NEGATIVE.text: Subtracting a quantity subtracts its rate of change too, so the sign can wait outside the derivative.

DIFF_CONSTANT_MULTIPLE.title: Move {constant} outside the derivative
DIFF_CONSTANT_MULTIPLE.text: Multiplying a function by {constant} stretches it by that factor, and stretching it stretches its slope by the same factor.

DIFF_CONSTANT_DENOMINATOR.title: Divide the derivative by {constant}
DIFF_CONSTANT_DENOMINATOR.text: Dividing by {constant} shrinks the function by a fixed factor, so it shrinks the slope by that same factor.

DIFF_PRODUCT.title: Use the product rule
DIFF_PRODUCT.text: Both {first} and {second} change with {variable}, so neither one can be held still while the other moves; each contributes a term.

DIFF_QUOTIENT.title: Use the quotient rule
DIFF_QUOTIENT.text: The bottom changes with {variable} as well as the top, so the two effects work against each other and the denominator gets squared.

DIFF_CONSTANT.title: The derivative of {constant} is zero
DIFF_CONSTANT.text: {constant} is the same number whatever {variable} does, so it has no rate of change.

DIFF_VARIABLE.title: Differentiate {variable}
DIFF_VARIABLE.text: {variable} keeps exact pace with itself, so its rate of change is 1.

DIFF_POWER.title: Use the power rule
DIFF_POWER.text: Bring the exponent {exponent} down in front and drop the power by one; that is the rate at which a power grows.

DIFF_CHAIN_POWER.title: Use the chain rule on the power
DIFF_CHAIN_POWER.text: The bracket is not just {variable}, so the power rule gives the outside rate and it has to be scaled by how fast the inside is moving.

DIFF_EXPONENTIAL.title: Differentiate the exponential
DIFF_EXPONENTIAL.text: An exponential grows in proportion to its own size, and the constant of proportionality for base {base} is the natural log of {base}.

DIFF_EXPONENTIAL_E.title: Differentiate the exponential
DIFF_EXPONENTIAL_E.text: e is the base whose exponential grows at exactly its own value, so only the rate of the exponent is left to account for.

DIFF_SIN.title: Differentiate the sine
DIFF_SIN.text: Sine is rising fastest where cosine is largest, so cosine measures its rate of change.

DIFF_SIN_CHAIN.title: Use the chain rule on the sine
DIFF_SIN_CHAIN.text: The angle {inside} is itself moving, so the usual cosine has to be scaled by how fast the angle changes.

DIFF_COS.title: Differentiate the cosine
DIFF_COS.text: Cosine falls while sine rises, so its rate of change is sine with a minus sign.

DIFF_COS_CHAIN.title: Use the chain rule on the cosine
DIFF_COS_CHAIN.text: The angle {inside} is itself moving, so the usual minus sine has to be scaled by how fast the angle changes.

DIFF_TAN.title: Differentiate the tangent
DIFF_TAN.text: Tangent steepens as it approaches a vertical asymptote, and secant squared is exactly how fast it steepens.

DIFF_TAN_CHAIN.title: Use the chain rule on the tangent
DIFF_TAN_CHAIN.text: The angle {inside} is itself moving, so secant squared has to be scaled by how fast the angle changes.

DIFF_EXP.title: Differentiate the exponential
DIFF_EXP.text: The exponential function is the one that grows at exactly its own value, so it is unchanged.

DIFF_EXP_CHAIN.title: Use the chain rule on the exponential
DIFF_EXP_CHAIN.text: The exponential still grows at its own value, but the exponent {inside} is moving too, so that rate multiplies in.

DIFF_LN.title: Differentiate the logarithm
DIFF_LN.text: The natural log climbs more slowly the bigger {variable} gets, at a rate of exactly one over {variable}.

DIFF_LN_CHAIN.title: Use the chain rule on the logarithm
DIFF_LN_CHAIN.text: The log measures relative change, so the rate is how fast {inside} moves compared with how big it already is.

DIFF_SQRT.title: Differentiate the square root
DIFF_SQRT.text: A square root flattens out as it grows, and the rate works out as one over twice the root.

DIFF_SQRT_CHAIN.title: Use the chain rule on the square root
DIFF_SQRT_CHAIN.text: The square root gives the outside rate, and it has to be scaled by how fast {inside} underneath is changing.

EVALUATE_TRIG.title: Read the exact value of {function}({angle})
EVALUATE_TRIG.text: {angle} is one of the angles whose {function} is known exactly, and it is {result} — not a rounded decimal.

EVALUATE_INVERSE_TRIG.title: Read the angle back
EVALUATE_INVERSE_TRIG.text: {result} is the angle in the principal range whose {function} counterpart gives {value}.

PYTHAGOREAN_IDENTITY.title: Use the Pythagorean identity
PYTHAGOREAN_IDENTITY.text: Sine and cosine of {angle} are the two legs of a right triangle with hypotenuse 1, so their squares always add to 1.

EVALUATE_LOG.title: Work out the logarithm
EVALUATE_LOG.text: A logarithm asks what power of {base} gives {argument}, and the answer here is exactly {result}.

LOG_PRODUCT.title: Add the logarithms
LOG_PRODUCT.text: Adding logarithms multiplies what is inside them, so {first} and {second} join into one logarithm.

LOG_QUOTIENT.title: Subtract the logarithms
LOG_QUOTIENT.text: Subtracting logarithms divides what is inside them, so {first} over {second} becomes a single logarithm.

LOG_POWER.title: Bring the exponent down
LOG_POWER.text: A power inside a logarithm is repeated multiplication, which a logarithm turns into repeated addition, so the {exponent} moves out in front.

LIMIT_SUBSTITUTE.title: Substitute {variable} = {point}
LIMIT_SUBSTITUTE.text: The expression is continuous here, so where it is heading is simply its value at {point}.

LIMIT_CONSTANT.title: The expression does not depend on {variable}
LIMIT_CONSTANT.text: Nothing inside changes as {variable} moves, so the limit is just {expression}.

LIMIT_INDETERMINATE.title: Substituting gives {form}
LIMIT_INDETERMINATE.text: {form} is indeterminate: it does not say the limit is 1, or 0, or anything at all. The expression has to be rewritten before {variable} = {point} can go in.

LIMIT_FACTOR.title: Factor out {factor}
LIMIT_FACTOR.text: Top and bottom are both zero at that point, which is exactly what it means for {factor} to divide into each of them; writing it out is what makes the cancelling visible.

LIMIT_AT_INFINITY.title: Compare the degrees
LIMIT_AT_INFINITY.text: The bottom is degree {bottom} and the top only degree {top}, so the denominator outgrows the numerator and the fraction is squeezed to zero.

LIMIT_AT_INFINITY_RATIO.title: Compare the degrees
LIMIT_AT_INFINITY_RATIO.text: Top and bottom are both degree {top}, so far out only the leading terms matter and the fraction settles at {result}.

LIMIT_LHOPITAL.title: Apply l'Hopital's rule
LIMIT_LHOPITAL.text: With the form {form}, what decides the limit is how fast {top} and {bottom} are changing, so differentiate each of them and ask again.

LIMIT_DOES_NOT_EXIST.title: The limit does not exist
LIMIT_DOES_NOT_EXIST.text: The expression does not settle on any value as {variable} approaches {point}, so there is no limit to report.

FACTOR_COMMON_FACTOR.title: Take out the common factor
FACTOR_COMMON_FACTOR.text: Every term is divisible by {factor}, so it can come outside a bracket.

FACTOR_DIFFERENCE_OF_SQUARES.title: Use the difference of two squares
FACTOR_DIFFERENCE_OF_SQUARES.text: This is {first} squared minus {second} squared, and a difference of squares always splits into a sum times a difference.

FACTOR_DIFFERENCE_OF_CUBES.title: Use the difference of two cubes
FACTOR_DIFFERENCE_OF_CUBES.text: This is {first} cubed minus {second} cubed, and the middle terms of the long bracket cancel when it is multiplied back out.

FACTOR_SUM_OF_CUBES.title: Use the sum of two cubes
FACTOR_SUM_OF_CUBES.text: This is {first} cubed plus {second} cubed, and the middle terms of the long bracket cancel when it is multiplied back out.

FACTOR_TRINOMIAL.title: Factor the trinomial
FACTOR_TRINOMIAL.text: Find two numbers that multiply to {product} and add to {sum}; they are the numbers that go in the brackets.

FACTOR_BY_GROUPING.title: Factor in pairs
FACTOR_BY_GROUPING.text: Neither pair factors on its own, but taking a factor out of each leaves the same bracket {shared} in both.

FACTOR_RATIONAL_ROOT.title: Divide out the factor for {variable} = {root}
FACTOR_RATIONAL_ROOT.text: The expression is zero at {variable} = {root}, so that bracket divides into it exactly.

FACTOR_OUT_VARIABLE.title: Take out {factor}
FACTOR_OUT_VARIABLE.text: There is no constant term, so {factor} is a factor of every term and one solution is zero.

RATIONAL_ROOT_CANDIDATES.title: List the possible whole-number roots
RATIONAL_ROOT_CANDIDATES.text: Any rational root is a factor of {constant} divided by a factor of {leading}, so only {candidates} are worth testing.

SYNTHETIC_DIVISION.title: Divide out the factor for {variable} = {root}
SYNTHETIC_DIVISION.text: Substituting {root} gives zero, so that bracket is a factor and dividing by it drops the degree by one.

LINEAR_FACTOR.title: Read off the last factor
LINEAR_FACTOR.text: What is left is linear, so it gives the remaining solution straight away.

ISOLATE_RADICAL.title: Get the root on its own
ISOLATE_RADICAL.text: Move {terms} across first; squaring only removes the root while it stands alone.

SQUARE_BOTH_SIDES.title: Square both sides
SQUARE_BOTH_SIDES.text: Squaring undoes the square root, but it can also create answers that do not fit the original, so they will have to be checked.

RAISE_BOTH_SIDES.title: Raise both sides to the power {index}
RAISE_BOTH_SIDES.text: Taking the power {index} undoes the root, at the cost of possibly creating answers the original does not have.

CHECK_EXTRANEOUS.title: Check each answer in the original equation
CHECK_EXTRANEOUS.text: Squaring is not reversible, so every candidate goes back in: {kept} works and {rejected} does not.

CHECK_NO_EXTRANEOUS.title: Check each answer in the original equation
CHECK_NO_EXTRANEOUS.text: Squaring can invent answers, so {candidates} goes back into the original, and it holds.

EXPONENTIAL_ALWAYS_POSITIVE.title: No solution
EXPONENTIAL_ALWAYS_POSITIVE.text: A positive number raised to any power stays positive, so it can never equal a number that is zero or negative.

MATCH_BASES.title: Write both sides as a power of {base}
MATCH_BASES.text: The right-hand side is {base} to the power {exponent}, so both sides can be compared directly.

EQUATE_EXPONENTS.title: Equate the exponents
EQUATE_EXPONENTS.text: Powers of {base} never repeat a value, so the two sides can only be equal when the exponents are.

TAKE_LOGARITHM.title: Take the logarithm of both sides
TAKE_LOGARITHM.text: The logarithm to base {base} is what undoes that power, and it brings the exponent down to where it can be solved for.

EXPONENTIATE_BOTH_SIDES.title: Write it without the logarithm
EXPONENTIATE_BOTH_SIDES.text: A logarithm to base {base} says what power {base} is raised to, so raising {base} to each side removes it.

REJECT_LOG_DOMAIN.title: Check each answer against the logarithms
REJECT_LOG_DOMAIN.text: A logarithm is only defined for a positive number, so {rejected} has to be thrown out and {kept} is left.

CHECK_LOG_DOMAIN.title: Check each answer against the logarithms
CHECK_LOG_DOMAIN.text: A logarithm is only defined for a positive number, and {kept} keeps every argument positive.

LOG_COEFFICIENT_TO_POWER.title: Move the multiplier into the logarithm
LOG_COEFFICIENT_TO_POWER.text: A multiple of a logarithm is the logarithm of that power, so {exponent} becomes the exponent of {argument}.

COMBINE_LOG_SUM.title: Combine the logarithms
COMBINE_LOG_SUM.text: Adding logarithms multiplies what is inside them, so {first} and {second} become one logarithm of their product.

COMBINE_LOG_DIFFERENCE.title: Combine the logarithms
COMBINE_LOG_DIFFERENCE.text: Subtracting logarithms divides what is inside them, so {first} and {second} become one logarithm of their quotient.

LOG_OF_POWER.title: Cancel the logarithm and the power
LOG_OF_POWER.text: A logarithm to base {base} of a power of {base} is just the exponent.

ABSOLUTE_NEVER_NEGATIVE.title: No solution
ABSOLUTE_NEVER_NEGATIVE.text: An absolute value measures distance, so it can never be negative.

ABSOLUTE_ALWAYS_GREATER.title: Every value works
ABSOLUTE_ALWAYS_GREATER.text: An absolute value is never negative, so it is greater than {value} wherever it is defined.

SPLIT_ABSOLUTE_VALUE.title: Split into two equations
SPLIT_ABSOLUTE_VALUE.text: {inner} is {value} away from zero, which happens on either side of it.

ABSOLUTE_LESS_THAN.title: Write it as one double inequality
ABSOLUTE_LESS_THAN.text: {inner} is less than {value} away from zero, so it lies between the two.

ABSOLUTE_GREATER_THAN.title: Split into two inequalities
ABSOLUTE_GREATER_THAN.text: {inner} is more than {value} away from zero, so it is beyond one end or the other and nothing in between works.

SOLVE_COMPOUND_INEQUALITY.title: Solve for {variable}
SOLVE_COMPOUND_INEQUALITY.text: The same operation applies to every part of the inequality at once.

MULTIPLY_BY_NEGATIVE.title: Multiply both sides by {by}
MULTIPLY_BY_NEGATIVE.text: Multiplying by a negative number reverses which side is larger, so the inequality turns round.

INEQUALITY_CRITICAL_POINTS.title: Find where the expression is zero
INEQUALITY_CRITICAL_POINTS.text: A polynomial can only change sign where it crosses zero, so {roots} divides the number line into the pieces to test.

INEQUALITY_TEST_INTERVALS.title: Test each interval
INEQUALITY_TEST_INTERVALS.text: Testing one value from each piece shows which of them satisfy the inequality.

INEQUALITY_ALWAYS_TRUE.title: Every value works
INEQUALITY_ALWAYS_TRUE.text: The parabola opens upwards and never dips below the axis, so nothing can fail the inequality.

INEQUALITY_NEVER_TRUE.title: No solution
INEQUALITY_NEVER_TRUE.text: The parabola opens upwards and never dips below the axis, so no value can make it negative.

INT_SUM.title: Integrate each term separately
INT_SUM.text: Area adds up term by term, so the {count} terms can be integrated one at a time.

INT_NEGATIVE.title: Take the minus sign outside
INT_NEGATIVE.text: Subtracting a quantity subtracts its area too, so the sign can wait outside the integral.

INT_CONSTANT_MULTIPLE.title: Move {constant} outside the integral
INT_CONSTANT_MULTIPLE.text: Stretching a function by {constant} stretches the area under it by the same factor, so the factor can come out.

INT_CONSTANT_DENOMINATOR.title: Divide the integral by {constant}
INT_CONSTANT_DENOMINATOR.text: Dividing the function by {constant} divides the area under it by {constant}, so the denominator can wait outside.

INT_CONSTANT.title: Integrate the constant {constant}
INT_CONSTANT.text: {constant} never changes, so the area under it grows in step with {variable}.

INT_POWER.title: Use the power rule
INT_POWER.text: Undo the power rule: raise the exponent from {exponent} to {raised} and divide by the new exponent.

INT_RECIPROCAL.title: Integrate one over {variable}
INT_RECIPROCAL.text: No power of {variable} differentiates to one over {variable}; the natural log does, and the absolute value covers the negative side too.

INT_EXPONENTIAL_E.title: Integrate the exponential
INT_EXPONENTIAL_E.text: e to the {variable} is its own derivative, so it is its own integral as well.

INT_EXPONENTIAL.title: Integrate the exponential
INT_EXPONENTIAL.text: Differentiating {base} to the {variable} multiplies it by the natural log of {base}, so integrating divides by it.

INT_SIN.title: Integrate the sine
INT_SIN.text: Cosine differentiates to minus sine, so sine integrates to minus cosine.

INT_COS.title: Integrate the cosine
INT_COS.text: Sine differentiates to cosine, so cosine integrates back to sine.

INT_SEC_SQUARED.title: Integrate secant squared
INT_SEC_SQUARED.text: Secant squared is exactly the derivative of the tangent, so it integrates straight back to it.

INT_ARCTAN.title: Recognise the arctangent
INT_ARCTAN.text: One over one plus {variable} squared is the derivative of the arctangent, so that is the area function.

INT_ARCSIN.title: Recognise the arcsine
INT_ARCSIN.text: One over the root of one minus {variable} squared is the derivative of the arcsine, so that is the area function.

INT_SUBSTITUTION.title: Substitute {placeholder} = {u}
INT_SUBSTITUTION.text: With {placeholder} = {u} the factor {rate} is exactly what d{placeholder} needs, and the integral becomes {inner} d{placeholder}, which integrates directly. Then {placeholder} goes back to {u}.

INT_LONG_DIVISION.title: Divide out the fraction first
INT_LONG_DIVISION.text: The top has at least the degree of the bottom, so divide to get {quotient} plus a smaller fraction, which is the part that needs work.

INT_PARTIAL_FRACTIONS.title: Split into partial fractions
INT_PARTIAL_FRACTIONS.text: The bottom factorises, so the fraction splits into {pieces} simpler ones, each of which integrates to a logarithm or a power.

INT_BY_PARTS.title: Integrate by parts
INT_BY_PARTS.text: Taking u = {u} and dv = {dv} gives v = {v} and du = {du}. The product rule run backwards trades this integral for {v} du, which is the easier one.

INT_EVALUATE_LIMITS.title: Evaluate at the limits
INT_EVALUATE_LIMITS.text: The area from {lower} to {upper} is the antiderivative at {upper} minus its value at {lower}.

INT_ADD_CONSTANT.title: Add the constant of integration
INT_ADD_CONSTANT.text: Every function differing by a constant has the same derivative, so the antiderivative is a whole family and C stands for which one.

INT_DEFINITE_SETUP.title: Find the antiderivative first
INT_DEFINITE_SETUP.text: Set the limits {lower} and {upper} aside, integrate as usual, and bring them back at the end.

INT_EXPAND.title: Multiply the brackets out first
INT_EXPAND.text: A polynomial has no shortcut worth keeping here, so expand it and integrate one term at a time.

DIFF_SEC.title: Differentiate the secant
DIFF_SEC.text: Secant is one over cosine, so it blows up exactly where cosine vanishes, and it climbs at secant times tangent.

DIFF_CSC.title: Differentiate the cosecant
DIFF_CSC.text: Cosecant is one over sine, and it falls where sine rises, which is the minus sign in front of cosecant times cotangent.

DIFF_COT.title: Differentiate the cotangent
DIFF_COT.text: Cotangent runs downhill everywhere it is defined, so its rate is minus cosecant squared.

DIFF_ARCSIN.title: Differentiate the inverse sine
DIFF_ARCSIN.text: Inverse sine is steepest at the ends of its domain, where one minus {variable} squared is smallest, and that root is what sits underneath.

DIFF_ARCCOS.title: Differentiate the inverse cosine
DIFF_ARCCOS.text: Inverse cosine falls wherever inverse sine rises, so it is the same rate with a minus sign in front.

DIFF_ARCTAN.title: Differentiate the inverse tangent
DIFF_ARCTAN.text: Inverse tangent flattens out as {variable} grows, and one over one plus {variable} squared is exactly how quickly it settles.

DIFF_SINH.title: Differentiate the hyperbolic sine
DIFF_SINH.text: The hyperbolic pair swap into each other, and sinh differentiates to cosh with no sign change.

DIFF_COSH.title: Differentiate the hyperbolic cosine
DIFF_COSH.text: cosh differentiates to sinh, and unlike the circular cosine it picks up no minus sign.

DIFF_TANH.title: Differentiate the hyperbolic tangent
DIFF_TANH.text: tanh settles towards its horizontal asymptotes, at a rate of one over cosh squared.

DIFF_LOG.title: Differentiate the base-ten logarithm
DIFF_LOG.text: A base-ten log is the natural log scaled down by ln 10, so its rate carries that same factor.

LIMIT_BOUNDED_OVER_UNBOUNDED.title: The bottom runs away, so the fraction goes to zero
LIMIT_BOUNDED_OVER_UNBOUNDED.text: {bottom} grows without any ceiling while the top stays put, so the fraction is a fixed amount shared among ever more, and it thins away to nothing.

INT_TAN.title: Integrate the tangent
INT_TAN.text: Tangent is sine over cosine, and the top is exactly what the bottom differentiates to apart from a sign, so the integral is minus the log of the cosine.

INT_COT.title: Integrate the cotangent
INT_COT.text: Cotangent is cosine over sine, and the top is what the bottom differentiates to, so the integral is the log of the sine.

INT_SIN_SQUARED.title: Use the half-angle identity on the square
INT_SIN_SQUARED.text: A squared sine has no antiderivative in the table, but sin squared equals one minus cos of twice the angle, over two — and that is a sum of things which do.

INT_COS_SQUARED.title: Use the half-angle identity on the square
INT_COS_SQUARED.text: A squared cosine has no antiderivative in the table, but cos squared equals one plus cos of twice the angle, over two — and that is a sum of things which do.

INT_SIN_ODD.title: Split off one sine and convert the rest
INT_SIN_ODD.text: An odd power leaves a single sine over once the rest is paired up, and the pairs become cosines through the Pythagorean identity, which sets up a substitution.

INT_COS_ODD.title: Split off one cosine and convert the rest
INT_COS_ODD.text: An odd power leaves a single cosine over once the rest is paired up, and the pairs become sines through the Pythagorean identity, which sets up a substitution.

INT_ARCTAN_SCALED.title: A scaled inverse tangent
INT_ARCTAN_SCALED.text: This is the inverse tangent form with {a} in place of one, so the answer carries a factor of one over {a} both inside and out.

ABS_OF_POSITIVE.title: Drop the absolute value
ABS_OF_POSITIVE.text: {value} is positive wherever it is defined, so the bars around it change nothing and can come off.

INT_IMPROPER_SETUP.title: Rewrite the infinite limit as a limit
INT_IMPROPER_SETUP.text: An area stretching out for ever is not something you can substitute into, so put {bound} where {infinite} was, work out the area up to {bound}, and then see where that total heads as {bound} runs off.

LIMIT_VANISHING_TERM.title: That term dies away to nothing
LIMIT_VANISHING_TERM.text: {term} shrinks towards zero as {variable} goes to {point}, so in the limit it contributes nothing and the rest of the sum is the whole answer.

INT_SEC.title: Integrate the secant
INT_SEC.text: Multiplying secant by (sec + tan) over itself makes the top the derivative of the bottom, and the integral falls out as the log of that sum.

INT_CSC.title: Integrate the cosecant
INT_CSC.text: The same trick as the secant, with (csc + cot), and the minus sign comes from cosecant falling where secant rises.

INT_COMPLETE_THE_SQUARE.title: Complete the square, then read the inverse tangent
INT_COMPLETE_THE_SQUARE.text: The bottom has no real roots, so it never vanishes. Writing it as {square} squared plus {a} squared puts it in the inverse tangent form, shifted along by {shift}.

INT_SQRT_AS_POWER.title: Write the root as a power
INT_SQRT_AS_POWER.text: {root} is {power}, and written that way the power rule can take it along with everything else it is multiplied by.

INT_EXPAND_POWERS.title: Multiply out first
INT_EXPAND_POWERS.text: Written as {expanded} this is a sum of separate powers, and the power rule takes each one on its own.

INT_CYCLIC_BY_PARTS.title: Integrate by parts twice and solve for the integral
INT_CYCLIC_BY_PARTS.text: Parts turns {integrand} into another integral of the same shape, and doing it again brings back the one you started with. So call the integral I, and the two rounds give an equation in I — rearranging it is what produces this answer, without ever integrating directly.

INT_TRIG_SUBSTITUTION.title: Substitute to clear the square root
INT_TRIG_SUBSTITUTION.text: Putting {substitution} turns {root} into {becomes}, because the Pythagorean identity collapses the root exactly. Integrate in {angle}, then read each function back off the right triangle the substitution describes.

INT_CSC_SQUARED.title: Integrate the cosecant squared
INT_CSC_SQUARED.text: Cotangent differentiates to minus cosecant squared, so cosecant squared integrates to minus cotangent.

INT_SEC_CUBED.title: The standard secant-cubed integral
INT_SEC_CUBED.text: Parts on secant cubed produces secant cubed again, so it is solved for rather than integrated — the same trick as a cyclic integration by parts, and this is the result.

INT_CSC_CUBED.title: The standard cosecant-cubed integral
INT_CSC_CUBED.text: The cosecant mirror of the secant-cubed result, reached the same way: parts brings the integral back and it is solved for.
